chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: Becoming the first white band at the Apollo in 1934
summary: Benny Carter recommended Barnet's Park Central band when Fletcher Henderson was unavailable, and Red Norvo's xylophone act went over.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Tell me about playing the Apollo. You're listed as the first[white] [inaudible] to play the Apollo theater in New York.
Well, that's true, unless you want to go back to the days when it was Hertig and Seamon's Burlesque
House and there was a white band in the pit then. But at that time the audience was mostly white.
How far back does that go?

Oh, that goes back into the '20s. But it's quite an old theater. It's been there for many, many years. Our first outing there at the Apollo was in 1934, and it came about more or less in an accidental way. Fletcher Henderson had broken up his band and Benny Carter had signed a contract to appear at the Apollo and he thought he was going to get -- believe it or not, there was a shortage, when I say competent black musicians, I mean guys that could read, you know. There was a lot of guys around that could play, but to play in a big band there was always a problem in those days to find guys that were capable of handling written arrangements in the discipline, you know, of a big band. And he was going to take the old Fletcher Henderson Band in there. Well, something happened. Fletcher decided to continue for another week or something and Benny was without a band. So the Apollo was hung up and Benny recommended us to -- this was before Frank Shiffman.] Frank Shiffman seems to have been forever there, but this was another guy that had this, the theater at the time. And Benny sold him on the idea of us playing there. And now this was the Park Central band, and we went up there and we were opened. Red Norvo, I had Red Norvo in the band. This is part of the Park Central band. I had Red Norvo doing his

thing with the xylophones and oh, he broke it up too, he really did. Of course you know Red was quite a performer before he became strictly a jazz player. I mean he was quite a showman. Did you ever see him chop that xylophone up? Well, he used to hit the xylophone. The climax to the whole thing is all the notes in the xylophone are -- he had a bunch of loose ones there, and they're flying all over the stage. It was sort of a comedy type thing.
